What if the Sun just blinked out, right now?
You wouldn't even know. Not for eight minutes and twenty seconds.
Then, lights out. Even the Moon goes dark.
No Sun to hold us? Earth flies off in a straight line.
At first, it drops thirty six degrees a day.
Three days in, almost everywhere is below freezing.
Ponds freeze in a week. Lakes, in months.
But under the ice, the oceans could stay liquid for years.
By hot sea vents, tiny life could live on rock chemicals, not sunlight.
Later, Earth gets colder than Pluto. Around minus four hundred degrees.
Enjoy that sunshine. It's eight minutes old. Subscribe for more what-ifs, before it blinks out.
